scene.title: Why am I pasting the same instructions into every chat?
scene.sceneHtml:
Maya's story: Week 2 – "Why am I pasting the same instructions into every chat?"

Maya was drafting quarterly client summaries for eight clients. Every chat started with the same 300-word block: "You are a client-success analyst. Our tone is professional with no contractions. Always include these five sections: Executive Summary, Metrics, Key Wins, Risks, Next Steps. Here is our terminology guide…"

Her manager said, "Set up a Project. Put those instructions in once, upload the terminology guide, and every chat in the Project gets them automatically. No more copy-paste." Maya created the "Quarterly Client Summaries" Project. Her prompts shrank from 400 words to 50, and every output followed the rules without her repeating them.

takeaways: A Project bundles custom instructions, uploaded knowledge and Skills; every chat in it inherits them. Use for recurring work, not one-offs.
When authoring custom instructions, define the Project's purpose and boundaries first, then draft, validate and refine them.
Fix weak Project output by being explicit: name the role, tone (no contractions), minimum length, required sections and attached policy.
Use a Skill by adding it, uploading knowledge and writing instructions that reference both. Review configs periodically as policies change.
